plan: To preserve capital, we will sell all leveraged ETFs like SOXL and SPAL.
We will also exit high-beta names such as PLTU, METU, MSFU, and MUU.
QQQI will be trimmed to 20% to meet the single name concentration limit.
This strategy prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a modest ~1.5% monthly return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged positions and high-beta names, leading to lower potential drawdowns.

plan: We will trim high-beta names like METU, MSFU, MUU, and PLTU to reduce risk.
Leveraged ETFs SOXL and SPAL will also be trimmed to maintain small exposure.
QQQI will be trimmed to 25% to comply with the single name concentration limit.
A new position in LMT will be initiated at 4% based on its strong scanner read.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% monthly growth, prioritizing risk management. It blends broad index exposure with quality tech and a small, controlled amount of leverage, aiming for moderate drawdowns.

plan: QQQI will be trimmed to 25% to adhere to the single name concentration limit.
We will add to high-beta names like METU, MSFU, MUU, and PLTU, increasing exposure.
Leveraged ETFs SOXL and SPAL will also be increased to 6% each.
A new position in LMT will be initiated at 6% based on its strong scanner read.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets a higher ~4% monthly return by leaning into leverage and concentration. Be aware that this significantly increases both upside potential and drawdown risk, especially with leveraged ETFs which experience daily decay and rebalancing. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: To prioritize income, we will sell all high-beta names like METU, MSFU, MUU, and PLTU.
All leveraged ETFs, including SOXL and SPAL, will be exited.
QQQI will be increased to 30% to boost monthly distribution potential.
This plan focuses on stable income over growth, with a lower drawdown profile.
income.read: This income plan aims for approximately 1% monthly distributions, prioritizing yield and low drawdown. While it seeks reliable income, distributions are variable and NAV can still decline in market downturns. This is not a savings account.
